author: EmuCore - Hub
title: Tune internal resolution for sustained PS2 emulation speed
summary: Test resolution multipliers through the heaviest known route, allow the device to reach steady temperature, require two long passes with headroom, and reject the highest opening-scene setting when late gameplay falls behind.
heroAlt: PCSX2 signal-sampling illustration representing the increasing pixel workload of higher internal resolution

blocks.text: Find the highest multiplier with late-session reserve

The correct internal resolution is not the largest value that renders a menu at full speed. Choose a route containing the most expensive known effects, wide views, and transitions. Begin at native output, keep renderer and accuracy fixed, and raise resolution one multiplier only after the prior level survives a warm run.
Do not reduce blending or accuracy while raising resolution. That can trade away required graphics correctness to finance sharper pixels.
Lock correctness before testing pixel cost

items: A verified graphics profile whose effects are already correct.
A ten-minute route containing the title's heaviest scene.
The same driver, renderer, power mode, brightness, and ambient conditions.
Native-resolution correctness and timing captures.
A target reserve below the device's first thermal decline.

blocks.text: Advance resolution one stable step at a time

items: 1. Cold-boot native resolution and complete the full route after warm-up.
2. Record speed and frame-time behavior at every heavy landmark.
3. Raise internal resolution one supported step and repeat from the same starting state.
4. Stop advancing when sustained speed misses target, frame-time spikes grow, or thermal decline arrives too early.
5. Return to the last passing multiplier and run the route twice.
6. Inspect HUD, post-processing, texture seams, and FMV for upscaling-specific artifacts.
7. Test one longer play segment beyond the route to confirm reserve.
8. Save the accepted multiplier in the title profile rather than globally.

blocks.text: Pixel cost often rises quickly with each multiplier, while mobile power and cooling remain limited. The last passing step with reserve is more useful than a marginal step that collapses after heat or a later effect. Correctness checks prevent resolution tuning from reintroducing graphics problems.
The selected multiplier must pass speed, heat, and image integrity together.

items: Two warm runs retain the title's target emulation speed.
The heaviest landmark keeps measurable headroom.
No new seams, offsets, or broken post-processing appear.
Thermal decline does not arrive inside normal play duration.
Another title can retain its own independent multiplier.
Only menus remain full speed: use the gameplay route.
A step passes cool but fails warm: return to the previous multiplier.
Graphics artifacts appear before performance loss: treat accuracy as the limiting boundary.
Changing renderer was required to pass: record that as a separate comparison.

blocks.text: Drop one multiplier without changing accuracy

Restore the last fully passing internal resolution, cold-boot the heavy route, and leave blending, patches, mipmapping, and driver untouched. Remove temporary global resolution overrides created during the test.
Display resolution does not equal internal resolution

Android may scale the final surface to the panel or external display. Internal resolution controls emulated rendering workload; output scaling and panel pixels are separate stages. Judge the setting in both a GPU-heavy scene and a fine-detail scene: the first establishes sustained headroom, while the second reveals whether text, thin geometry, and distant texture detail remain acceptable. Record the chosen multiplier per game rather than assuming the phone panel resolution is a useful universal target.
